outlook: USDA's October reports surprised the trade by raising the U.S. corn yield 2.7 bushels to 181.2 bu/acre, lifting the crop to about 16.03 billion bushels and 2026-27 ending stocks to 1.849 billion — roughly 180 million above what analysts expected. December corn fell close to its 30-cent daily limit after the 11 am CT release and settled 19¾ cents lower at $4.80½. USDA put the soybean yield at a record 53.1 bu/acre with ending stocks up 5 million to 315 million; November beans dropped as much as 16 cents before recovering to close about 4¾ cents higher at $12.92¼. Wheat ending stocks rose to 740 million on a 25-million-bushel export cut (hard red spring stocks were trimmed 8 million), and December Chicago wheat lost 12½ cents while Minneapolis December spring wheat fell 10¾ cents to $6.95¼; ICE canola edged up C$1 to C$816.90. Minneapolis cash bids shown are from Thursday's final USDA report, before today's drop in corn and wheat futures.
